lead: "The two-day program with an overnight stay on King George Island includes a flight from Punta Arenas, visits to polar stations, penguins on Ardley Island and an insulated camp near Collins Glacier. Accommodation arrangements, the mandatory briefing and extra time in Chile are important considerations."
---

## Two days in Antarctica with an overnight stay near Collins Glacier

**The highlight of this tour is a night in an equipped field camp on King George Island itself.** After flying from [Punta Arenas](/chile/place/punta-arenas/), participants spend the day among scientific stations and Antarctic shores, then stay overnight at a camp near [Collins Glacier](/antarctica/place/collins-glacier/). The following day, they explore other parts of the island and fly back to Chile.

Unlike the [one-day air excursion](/antarctica/tour/antarctica-day-tour-from-punta-arenas/), this program adds an evening and a morning on the island. Compared with the [eight-day air-cruise](/antarctica/tour/classic-antarctica-air-cruise-8-days/), it offers less time sailing but includes an overnight stay on Antarctic land.

## Where the group goes on the first day

After landing on [King George Island](/antarctica/place/king-george-island/), participants are met by a guide. The itinerary covers several distinct sites, each revealing a different aspect of island life:

- [Villa Las Estrellas](/antarctica/place/villa-las-estrellas/) — a Chilean settlement associated with everyday life under polar conditions.
- [Bellingshausen Station](/antarctica/place/bellingshausen-station/) — a Russian base with an Orthodox church nearby.
- [Ardley Island](/antarctica/place/ardley-island/) — the destination of a Zodiac boat trip to a penguin colony.
- [Collins Glacier](/antarctica/place/collins-glacier/) — the destination of another boat outing and a landmark for the overnight camp.

The second day includes visits to the elephant seal colony area known as Elefanteras and China's [Great Wall Station](/antarctica/place/great-wall-station/). Additional places may be accessible depending on the weather. The local team decides the sequence of outings and whether each visit can take place.

Choose this program for the combination of these experiences. Penguins and elephant seals live in their natural habitat: neither their exact numbers nor how close you will get can be guaranteed.

## What the overnight polar camp is like

The camp near Collins Glacier has **3 small insulated sleeping modules, each accommodating 2 people**. A separate dining module and a sanitary tent with a basic toilet are also provided. This is field accommodation, not a hotel room with its own shower and the usual amenities.

The group is small, with **5 to 6 passengers per flight**. The aircraft named for this program is a Beechcraft King Air 300. The small group creates an intimate experience, although all movements depend on the guide, weather conditions and site access rules.

A night by the glacier is especially appealing to travelers who want to experience Antarctica beyond a few daytime stops. However, the field conditions, cold and limited infrastructure require readiness for expedition life. The program does not describe a separate, comfortable alternative with **hotel accommodation on the island itself**.

## Preparation in Punta Arenas takes additional time

The Antarctic portion lasts **2 days / 1 night**. The Chilean part of the trip also includes **4 nights at the Cabo de Hornos hotel or another hotel of the same category**. The full travel calendar therefore needs to be agreed before purchasing international flights: the short advertised duration is not the total number of nights away.

The mandatory briefing on the day before departure is particularly important. Participants must arrive in Punta Arenas **no later than 17:00 on the day before the trip**. Passengers who miss the briefing are not allowed to board the flight. A late connection via Santiago can be decisive even for a two-day Antarctic program.

The price includes transfers, accommodation and meals along the route, as well as round-trip flights between Punta Arenas and Antarctica. International flights to the departure city, additional meals and personal expenses are not included.

## What to consider before visiting the penguins and glacier

On King George Island, wildlife observation restrictions must be followed. Visitors may not approach birds or elephant seals so closely that the animals change their behavior; feeding wildlife and leaving litter are prohibited. Follow your guides' instructions both aboard the boat and ashore.

Visiting the glacier area does not mean you can walk independently on the ice field. Glaciers can contain hidden crevasses, so going onto the ice without special arrangements and permission is prohibited.

A sensible packing plan includes warm layers, waterproof outerwear, gloves and preparation for wind. Check the baggage allowance for the small aircraft and your insurance terms in advance. The tour text does not support a promise that all equipment will be provided free of charge.

## How weather affects the overnight stay and return flight

Takeoffs and landings depend on weather at both ends of the route. Wind and swell may cancel a particular Zodiac outing, while runway conditions may change flight times. Allow some flexibility when planning independent connections for the day after your return.

Ada Tours helps coordinate the sequence of the trip, arrival time and onshore preparations for this program. When booking, check the actual number of hotel nights and the arrangements in the event of a weather delay; these details cannot be inferred from the tour's short name.

Other ways to explore the region include the [Antarctica tour catalog](/antarctica/tour/) and [nature trips focused on Antarctic wildlife](/interests/wildlife/tours/antarctica/).

## Frequently asked questions about overnight stays in Antarctica

### Where exactly do guests stay overnight?

At a specially equipped camp near Collins Glacier on King George Island, in insulated two-person modules.

### How many people stay in one sleeping module?

Each module accommodates 2 people. There are 3 sleeping modules in total, plus separate dining and sanitary tents.

### Is arriving in Chile on the day of the Antarctic flight enough?

No. The mandatory briefing takes place the day before, and you must reach Punta Arenas by 17:00 on the preceding day.

### Can every stop on the island be promised in advance?

No. Visits ashore, Zodiac outings and the flight home depend on safe weather and local conditions.

lead: >-
  The program with an overnight stay on King George Island starts in Punta Arenas, Chile. The tour lasts 5 days and 4 nights, including one night in an ice camp on the island. After the flight, travelers visit scientific stations, take a Zodiac boat to a penguin colony and spend the night at Collins Glacier. Before booking, the most important considerations are tent accommodation, the mandatory briefing and the dependence of flights on weather.
---

## Antarctica overnight: how this trip differs from a one-day flight

The main difference is the chance to **spend the night on an Antarctic island itself**. The journey starts in [Punta Arenas](/chile/place/punta-arenas/), where the group boards a flight to [King George Island](/antarctica/place/king-george-island/). After exploring nearby attractions, travelers stay overnight in an ice camp and continue their excursions the next day.

The tour lasts **5 days and 4 nights**, including 3 nights in Punta Arenas and 1 night on King George Island. The 2 Antarctic sightseeing days are therefore not the full duration of the vacation. Before the flight, participants must arrive in Chile, check into their accommodation and attend a mandatory preparatory meeting.

For comparison, consider the [one-day program from Punta Arenas](/antarctica/tour/antarctica-day-tour-from-punta-arenas/). If a longer sea expedition is more important, explore other [Antarctica tours](/antarctica/tour/). A fly-in visit with a night on land differs from several days aboard a ship in both activities and living conditions.

## What a night in the ice camp involves

After the day's visits, the group is taken to the camp at [Collins Glacier](/antarctica/place/collins-glacier/), approximately 6 km from the airstrip. The accommodation is described as **3 insulated tent modules**, each designed for 3–6 people. Another module serves as a communal dining area, and a separate tent provides a basic toilet.

This is field accommodation, not a hotel room. Before booking, clarify how participants are assigned to tents, what bedding is provided and which personal items you need. Space for changing clothes and storing luggage in a confined area also matters.

Hotel accommodation is provided in Punta Arenas; the program names the Cabo de Hornos hotel or one of the same category. **Conditions at the mainland hotel do not apply to the night on the glacier.** This distinction matters particularly when comparing two short Antarctic trips.

Spending a night beneath the polar sky is attractive in itself, but weather, wind and limited creature comforts make it a choice to consider carefully. If familiar hotel standards matter, compare the overnight program with options without a camp before discussing flights.

## What the Antarctic portion includes

The first day on the island includes visits to Villa Las Estrellas, a Chilean settlement, and the area around Russia's Bellingshausen Station with its Orthodox church. The group then takes a Zodiac boat to [Ardley Island](/antarctica/place/ardley-island/) and its penguin colony. Another activity is a boat trip toward [Collins Glacier](/antarctica/place/collins-glacier/).

The following day includes the elephant seal colony area called Elefanteras and China's Great Wall Station. After the excursions, the group is scheduled to fly back to Punta Arenas.

This journey explores a particular part of Antarctica, chiefly the King George Island area. It **does not involve a multi-day sea crossing of the Drake Passage**. Zodiac boats are used locally for short outings and observation, not for travel from Chile to Antarctica.

Wildlife interactions are restricted by conservation rules. Penguins and elephant seals must not be fed, touched or chased for photographs. The boat's route, the distance from colonies and whether landings can take place depend on weather conditions and the guides' instructions.

## Weather dependence and allowing extra time

Flying to King George Island avoids a multi-day ship crossing, but the air portion is particularly sensitive to weather. The tour conditions explicitly state that weather affects **flights, landings, boat navigation and access to individual sites**.

On the island, the order or duration of visits may change, and a particular colony or station may become inaccessible. Photographs help you imagine the places, but they do not guarantee that every stop will be available on your chosen date.

Before booking international return flights, agree on a time buffer after the planned return to Punta Arenas. Also ask about the rules in the event of a delay: which additional nights and meals are provided, who pays for an extended stay and how flights are rescheduled. This program page does not state universal compensation terms, so they should not be assumed.

## Mandatory briefing in Punta Arenas

The guide meets participants in Punta Arenas and conducts a briefing before the Antarctic portion. The trip conditions require travelers to arrive in the city **by 17:00 on the day before departure**; anyone who misses the briefing will not be allowed on the flight.

Keep this rule in mind when planning connections. An international flight, hotel check-in and group meeting all take time. Even a convenient late flight may be unsuitable if it prevents attendance at the required preparation.

Check the clothing and footwear list before departure as well. Protection against wind and moisture is essential for polar landings, as is clean equipment: shoes, clothing and bags must not carry soil, seeds or other foreign material into Antarctica. Biosecurity requirements and visitor rules guide the local team's work.

## Who will enjoy this way of seeing Antarctica

This program appeals to travelers who want time ashore, visits to research stations, wildlife observation and the experience of a night in a field camp. Choose it for the experience of staying on the island rather than for the highest possible number of geographic stops.

Travelers must be prepared for cold, uncertain weather, boat outings and sharing a sleeping module with other participants. Individual medical restrictions, insurance and evacuation arrangements should be discussed before the trip. In this remote polar area, medical help cannot be expected to be as accessible as in a major city.

If a longer ship-based expedition is the priority, compare [Antarctica cruises and expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/tours/antarctica/). For a shorter look at the colonies and island without sleeping on the glacier, consider the [one-day fly-in option](/antarctica/tour/antarctica-day-tour-from-punta-arenas/).

## Frequently asked questions about an Antarctic overnight stay

### Where does the group sleep?

On King George Island, in an ice camp at Collins Glacier. The description specifies insulated tent modules sleeping 3–6 people, a shared dining module and a separate sanitary module.

### Is a ship crossing of the Drake Passage necessary?

No. The itinerary includes flights from Punta Arenas to King George Island and back. Zodiac boats are used for local navigation around the Antarctic island.

### Can I skip the preflight briefing?

No. The preparatory meeting is mandatory for permission to board under the program's conditions, so you must arrive in Punta Arenas in advance.

### What if the weather changes the departure time?

Coordinate with the organizer and follow the program leaders' instructions. Obtain the specific terms for rescheduling, additional nights and expenses when booking: the program confirms that weather can affect the schedule but does not promise identical compensation in every situation.

## Expedition to the Antarctic Circle: what the 13-day itinerary includes

The journey, **March 6–18, 2027**, begins in [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) and crosses the Drake Passage toward the Antarctic Peninsula. The aim of the southern part of the route is to approach the Antarctic Circle and, if ice conditions allow, cross it. **Crossing the Circle is not guaranteed:** in Antarctica, the expedition team chooses a safe course according to the current weather and ice conditions.

The program lasts **13 days and 12 nights**. The first and last days are connected with Ushuaia, the Drake Passage crossings fall on days 2–3 and 11–12, and the Antarctic portion is planned for days 4–10. This journey suits travelers prepared to spend several days on the open ocean for the chance to land ashore, enjoy glacier scenery and observe polar wildlife.

To compare other travel formats, browse [Antarctica tours](/antarctica/tour/) and [cruises and expeditions](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/). The main criteria here are the length of the Antarctic portion and the journey south, rather than a promised number of islands.

## From Ushuaia to the Antarctic Peninsula

After sailing through the Beagle Channel, the ship heads for the Drake Passage. The two-day crossing brings opportunities to watch seabirds, but weather and waves can make it challenging even for experienced travelers. Continuing south, the vessel crosses the Antarctic Convergence, where cold Antarctic waters meet subantarctic waters.

On the peninsula, the expedition plans to combine observation from the deck with Zodiac boat outings. **Possible**, rather than mandatory, stops include Deception Island, Neko Harbour, Paradise Harbour, the Lemaire Channel, Pléneau Island and Petermann Island. Landings may be possible in some places if shore conditions permit.

The route also envisages sailing along the Argentine Islands toward Crystal Sound and attempting to cross the Antarctic Circle. Historic sites mentioned include the former British research station on Detaille Island. The exact order of these visits is decided during the voyage.

## March in Antarctica: wildlife, ice and daylight

March comes at the end of the Antarctic summer. During this period, humpback whales, penguins, leopard seals and many seabirds may be seen. Growing penguin chicks head toward the sea, and whales feed in krill-rich waters before migrating.

Wildlife sightings depend on animal behavior and the sailing area. A particular species cannot be promised on a particular day; the same applies to rare atmospheric phenomena and any mention of the southern lights.

The expedition format differs from a standard ocean cruise: landings and boat outings depend on wind, swell, ice conditions and environmental regulations. Travelers follow the expedition team's instructions and rules on keeping a safe distance from wildlife.

## Choosing a cabin and preparing for departure

The main program includes a table of **five cabin categories with prices stated as "from"**. However, the final price, currency, specific vessel, cabin availability and included services must be confirmed before booking. There is no basis for assuming that meals, landing equipment, guiding language or additional activities are automatically included.

Practical considerations include medical readiness for the sea crossing, protection from wind and moisture, warm layered clothing and the ability to climb down into a boat independently if required for a particular landing. Extra activities, including diving, are available only when their conditions are confirmed for the program.

When arranging flights to Argentina, allow extra time before boarding the ship and after returning to Ushuaia. In adverse weather, the duration of individual crossings may differ from the original plan.

## Frequently asked questions about the expedition beyond the Antarctic Circle

### Is crossing the Antarctic Circle guaranteed?

No. It is the expedition's objective, achieved only if ice conditions and safe navigation permit.

### What departure dates does the program specify?

March 6–18, 2027, **13 days and 12 nights**, beginning and ending in Ushuaia.

### Which landings are guaranteed?

There is no fixed list of guaranteed landings. The program identifies possible islands and bays, while the expedition team makes the actual decisions.

### Are the price and vessel name confirmed?

Five cabin options are listed, but the currency, final price, vessel and included services need confirmation before booking.

## Antarctica for the whales: what the March expedition offers

Whale watching is the main nature theme of this 11-day sea expedition. The ship departs from [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), follows the [Beagle Channel](/argentina/place/beagle-channel/), spends two days crossing the [Drake Passage](/antarctica/place/drake-passage/) and operates in Antarctic waters near the [peninsula](/antarctica/place/antarctic-peninsula/). The return journey also crosses the Drake Passage and ends in Ushuaia.

The voyage lasts **11 days and 10 nights**. Two departures are published: **March 7–17 and March 17–27, 2027**. Days 4–8 form a single Antarctic portion in the itinerary, with the exact observation areas determined by the shipboard team. This is crucial for expectations: the journey focuses on whales, but their appearance, the number of sightings and opportunities to approach them cannot be guaranteed in advance.

The key difference from the [general discovery expedition](/antarctica/tour/antarctica-discovery-learning-11-days/) is the main theme. On that voyage, attention is spread among islands, glaciers, birds and possible landings. Here the route is presented primarily as an introduction to Antarctica through whale watching and marine nature.

## How much time is allotted to observation

| Period | Main activity |
|---|---|
| Day 1 | Departure from Ushuaia |
| Days 2–3 | Southbound crossing of the Drake Passage |
| Days 4–8 | Expedition in Antarctic waters |
| Days 9–10 | Return sea crossing |
| Day 11 | Disembarkation in Ushuaia |

The voyage has **five calendar days in the Antarctic portion**, but this does not mean five full days of guaranteed whale watching. Weather windows, the ship's movements, ice conditions and the animals' natural behavior determine the actual schedule.

Whales may already be encountered in the Drake Passage on the way south. Other seabirds listed for this part of the route include albatrosses, Cape petrels and other petrels. Marine life changes as the vessel crosses the Antarctic Convergence. Even when large marine mammals are far from the ship, this leg offers opportunities to observe the ocean, birds and the gradual approach to Antarctic waters.

Possible route areas include the Melchior Islands, Schollaert Channel and the waters between Brabant and Anvers islands. Days 5–8 are not tied to specific guaranteed bays. This voyage is best chosen for the **observation period and general geography**, rather than a precise schedule for each outing.

## Responsible whale watching

Wild whales move freely. They may be seen at a distance from the ship or, in favorable conditions, closer to it; sometimes a sighting is very brief. Reports of previous encounters should therefore be treated as examples, not as promises for the next voyage.

IAATO's general guidance for vessels near marine mammals centers on respect for animal behavior: **whales must not be chased, made to change direction, fed or touched**. The captain and expedition team are responsible for safe vessel movements and restrictions in each situation. If a whale swims away, observation ends or continues from a distance appropriate to the conditions.

Before booking, ask which open decks are used for observation and what expedition activities are actually included in your departure. **Zodiac outings, a specific number of sightings and specialist sessions with a biologist have not yet been confirmed as included services.** Do not assume that offers from similar ships or operators apply to this program.

## How the March departures differ when choosing a trip

The expedition has two consecutive date ranges in March 2027. This provides a choice for vacation planning but does not promise identical natural conditions on both departures. Sea state, wind, visibility, drifting ice and whale locations change through the season.

We cannot promise a particular species or number of whales. Before selecting a date, ask about the actual vessel, route and onboard decision-making practices. If you care more about specific coastal areas, compare this voyage with other [Antarctic expeditions](/antarctica/tour/) and see which landings are listed in their programs.

Travel to [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) is planned separately from the ship's itinerary. Ushuaia is the embarkation and disembarkation city; international and domestic flights to the port should be coordinated so that a late arrival does not risk missing departure. It is wise to leave a buffer before your return flight: expedition schedules are sensitive to sea conditions.

## What to bring for watching from the deck

For an Antarctic departure in March, prepare for cold wind, damp conditions and long periods near open water. The practical priority is keeping warm even while standing on deck and scanning the horizon for a long time. Wear layers, a windproof outer shell, a hat, warm gloves and nonslip footwear that meets the vessel's rules.

Binoculars help reveal distant movement on the water. Protect your camera from spray and condensation. Avoid heavy optics that are difficult to hold securely on a moving deck. If photographing wildlife, use short bursts and do not pursue a perfect shot at any cost: an encounter may last only a few minutes.

Conservation rules apply on Antarctic shores. Leaving no belongings or traces, following briefings and protecting wildlife are part of normal expedition conduct. Boarding small boats and landing, if provided for a particular departure, also depend on sea conditions and the crew's decisions.

## Cabins and costs: what can be compared before confirming a booking

Five options are listed for this voyage: Porthole Twin, Porthole Triple, Porthole Quad, Twin Window and Twin Deluxe. They differ in stated occupancy and the type of window or porthole. Each category is priced **per person**, but the currency and final price must be confirmed; it would be wrong to present the figures as US dollars without confirmation.

Request the cabin plan, vessel name, meals included, language of guiding, possible extra charges and terms for expedition changes in advance. A detailed list of included and excluded services is not yet provided. Do not assume pre-embarkation accommodation, port transfers, boot rental or special outings are included in the published rates.

| Question | What to confirm |
|---|---|
| Accommodation | Berth, cabin and its category |
| Currency | Per-person calculation and final total |
| Vessel | Specific departure and cabin plan |
| Activities | Confirmed landings and sessions |
| Changes | Procedures in case of weather restrictions |

The whale-watching theme does not replace these details. It is especially important to confirm in writing how the expedition portion will be organized in unfavorable weather. If you want to combine a sea voyage with more demanding shore activities, consider the [long-hike itinerary](/antarctica/tour/antarctica-discovery-long-hikes-11-days/) and its additional restrictions.

## Who should choose this particular voyage

The March program suits travelers for whom seeing a whale is a major personal goal, while the trip still has value without such a sighting: ocean birds, icy islands, the Antarctic Peninsula and the experience of an expedition in natural conditions remain part of the journey.

If the goal is to be guaranteed a particular trail, bay or number of landings, this program should not be judged by such promises. The expedition centers on the chance to observe wildlife in its natural habitat. Related options are collected in the [Antarctica nature-trip catalog](/interests/wildlife/tours/antarctica/).

## Frequently asked questions about the whale expedition

### Is whale watching guaranteed every day?

No. The program includes five days in Antarctic waters, but sightings depend on animal behavior, the ship's route and weather. There is no separate schedule of guaranteed encounters.

### Why does the trip last 11 days if whales are the main goal?

Two days are allotted to the southbound Drake Passage crossing and another two to the return. The first and last days are connected with Ushuaia. The Antarctic portion therefore falls on days 4–8, and ocean crossings make up a significant part of the journey.

### Should I choose a departure based on a particular whale species?

There is no basis for promising a particular species: the published program does not guarantee such encounters. Choose according to route, dates, vessel conditions and your willingness to accept the natural uncertainty of wildlife watching.

### Does the tour include outings in small boats?

This cannot be confirmed from the currently published list of services. Ask whether Zodiac outings are included and under what conditions for the specific March departure if they matter to you.

## Classic Antarctica: why choose an eight-day air-cruise

**The main feature of this program is flying to Antarctica before sailing aboard an expedition vessel.** Participants depart from Chile's [Punta Arenas](/chile/place/punta-arenas/) for [King George Island](/antarctica/place/king-george-island/), then take a Zodiac boat to the ship. The following days are spent among icebergs and fjords along the western coast of the [Antarctic Peninsula](/antarctica/place/antarctic-peninsula/).

This route avoids the long sea crossing of the Drake Passage from South America. However, it remains a genuine cruise, with maritime weather, nights on board, excursion boats and a flexible landing plan. Travelers who only want a brief visit to the island may prefer a [short fly-in trip](/antarctica/tour/antarctica-day-tour-from-punta-arenas/); this tour is designed as a multi-day expedition.

## Itinerary: which days are for flights and exploration

| Days | Main activity |
|---|---|
| 1 | Punta Arenas and briefing |
| 2 | King George Island, embarkation |
| 3–6 | Cruise and shore excursions |
| 7 | Flight back to Chile |
| 8 | Airport transfer |

On the first day, you must arrive in Punta Arenas **before 14:00**. The program includes a meeting, accommodation, a mandatory briefing at the Explorers House and a welcome dinner. This is a full preparation day, so a connection arriving late does not meet the published conditions.

After the flight to King George Island, participants walk about **2 km** through the area of Chile's [Frei Station](/antarctica/place/frei-station/) and Russia's [Bellingshausen Station](/antarctica/place/bellingshausen-station/). The group is then taken to the expedition ship by Zodiac. Comfortable footwear and wind protection are needed from the day of arrival on the island.

The main cruise takes place on days 3–6. Day 7 is scheduled for the return to King George Island and the flight to Punta Arenas. After a night on the mainland, an airport transfer is provided on day 8.

## What you might see during the voyage

The travel area includes the South Shetland Islands and the western coast of the [Antarctic Peninsula](/antarctica/place/antarctic-peninsula/). Possible route sections include Antarctic Sound, Gerlache Strait and Penola Strait.

These are **possible expedition routes**, not a guaranteed list of landings. Ice, wind, swell and coastal conditions change the ship's options every day. The expedition team chooses where landings can be made safely and which bays to explore by boat. Choose this program for several days among varied Antarctic landscapes, not for a mandatory visit to a particular strait.

Penguins, seals, seabirds and whales may be encountered during the voyage. Sightings depend on the season and animal behavior, so a specific number cannot be promised. For a comparison of nature-focused programs, browse the [Antarctica wildlife-trip selection](/interests/wildlife/tours/antarctica/).

## Zodiac landings and life aboard the ship

Daily Zodiac outings are planned during the expedition portion. Polar guides accompany participants ashore. The landing areas may be snowy or rocky, making balance, warm clothing and following crew instructions important. Landings may be postponed or changed if conditions become unsafe.

Lectures and talks about Antarctica take place aboard the ship. Between outings, travelers can watch glaciers and marine animals from the deck or observation lounges. This format combines polar exploration with time to learn about what has been seen. Other sea voyages appear in the [cruises and expeditions catalog](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/tours/antarctica/).

Conservation rules apply to every landing: do not feed animals, approach them so closely that their behavior changes, remove natural objects or leave litter. Participants must not leave the group or designated route without the guide's permission.

## Included services and expenses outside the cruise

The tour includes round-trip flights from Punta Arenas to King George Island, the cruise, guided shore excursions, meals aboard the ship, some drinks with lunches and dinners, hot beverages and snacks. **Waterproof boots** are provided for landings. The land portion includes **1 hotel night with breakfast after returning from Antarctica** and group transfers at the end of the voyage.

Personal insurance, additional accommodation and excursions, meals after returning to Punta Arenas, bar purchases, communications, laundry, tips and visa expenses are not included. Compare the specific services of your booking with this program rather than automatically assuming the terms of other expeditions apply.

When budgeting, include travel to Punta Arenas and back. Extra hotel nights and your own international flights must be calculated separately.

## Why an air-cruise still needs a time buffer

Flying shortens the journey by avoiding the Drake Passage, but weather dependence remains. Landing conditions on the island, wind, cloud cover and sea state affect flights and shore visits. Do not arrange an international connection home on the assumption that the return from Antarctica cannot be delayed.

The expedition requires warm layers, waterproof and windproof outerwear, gloves, headwear and protection for belongings against moisture. Baggage rules for the flight portion and the equipment list must be checked separately. The boots included in the services do not mean that a complete clothing set is provided.

If a night **on the island itself** matters more than several days on a ship, compare the [camp program near Collins Glacier](/antarctica/tour/antarctica-overnight-adventure/). Its accommodation and route are entirely different.

## Frequently asked questions about the classic air-cruise

### Do I need to cross the Drake Passage by ship?

No. The group flies to King George Island and boards the expedition vessel there. The sea portion takes place around the Antarctic Peninsula.

### How many days are spent on the expedition itself?

After flying and embarking on day 2, the main sea program is planned for days 3–6. The remaining days are for preparation and travel.

### Are all the listed landing sites guaranteed?

No. The straits and islands indicate possible geography. Actual outings depend on weather, ice and the expedition team's decisions.

### Is personal insurance included?
